knowledge:
- key_parameters: train.expr.set=An ExpressionSet object containing the training microarray expression data ;; test.expr.set=An ExpressionSet object containing the test microarray expression data ;; trainClass=A vector of binary class labels (0 or 1) for the training samples ;; testClass=A vector of binary class labels (0 or 1) for the test samples ;; p=The number of top BSS/WSS ranked genes to use in the iterative process (e.g., 100) ;; postprobArr=A vector of posterior probabilities of the selected models, used in prediction ;; mleArr=A matrix of maximum likelihood estimates of coefficients for each model, used in prediction
- alternatives: Traditional BMA (using bic.glm from the BMA package directly) is limited to datasets where the number of variables is less than the number of responses (or max 30 variables due to leaps and bounds algorithm inefficiency). Single-model gene selection methods ignore model uncertainty and use a single set of genes, whereas BMA averages over multiple models.
- when_to_use: Use this package when performing binary (2-class) classification and gene selection on high-dimensional transcriptomics/microarray data where the number of genes greatly exceeds the number of samples, and you want to account for model uncertainty.
- pitfalls: The algorithm is specifically designed for binary (2-class) classification problems; multi-class classification is not supported by these functions. Input data must be formatted as ExpressionSet objects, and class labels must be binary (0, 1). The traditional BMA step is computationally inefficient for more than 30 variables, which is why the iterative windowing approach (with maxNvar = 30) is strictly required.

workflows.name: microarray_binary_classification
workflows.intent: Perform gene selection and binary classification on microarray expression data using iterative Bayesian Model Averaging.
input: trainData (ExpressionSet containing training sample gene expression)
trainClass (vector of binary class labels 0/1 for training samples)
testData (ExpressionSet containing test sample gene expression)
testClass (vector of binary class labels 0/1 for test samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the training and test ExpressionSet data and class labels ;; 2. Train the iterative BMA model to select relevant genes using iterateBMAglm.train ;; 3. Extract selected genes and model posterior probabilities ;; 4. Predict class probabilities for test samples using bma.predict ;; 5. Evaluate prediction accuracy using brier.score ;; 6. Alternatively, perform training and prediction in a single step using iterateBMAglm.train.predict or iterateBMAglm.train.predict.test ;; 7. Visualize selected genes and models using imageplot.iterate.bma
workflows.code:
library ("Biobase")
library("BMA")
library("iterativeBMA")

data(trainData)
data(trainClass)

ret.bic.glm <- iterateBMAglm.train (train.expr.set=trainData, trainClass, p=100)
ret.bic.glm$namesx
ret.bic.glm$probne0

ret.gene.names <- ret.bic.glm$namesx[ret.bic.glm$probne0 > 0]
ret.gene.names

ret.bic.glm$postprob

data (testData)

curr.test.dat <- t(exprs(testData)[ret.gene.names,])

y.pred.test <- apply (curr.test.dat, 1, bma.predict, postprobArr=ret.bic.glm$postprob, mleArr=ret.bic.glm$mle)

data (testClass)
brier.score (y.pred.test, testClass)

ret.vec <- iterateBMAglm.train.predict (train.expr.set=trainData, test.expr.set=testData, trainClass, p=100)

data (testClass)
brier.score (ret.vec, testClass)

iterateBMAglm.train.predict.test (train.expr.set=trainData, test.expr.set=testData, trainClass, testClass, p=100)

imageplot.iterate.bma (ret.bic.glm)
